question: What shapes a patient's decision to seek medical help?

options.A: The exact number of hospital beds
options.B: The brand of soap used at home
options.C: The color of their clinic uniform

explanation: A person's background, culture, and social network heavily influence how they view illness and decide to visit a healthcare facility. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why must nurses look beyond the immediate biological disease?

options.A: To diagnose rare surgical complications faster
options.B: To understand the patient's everyday reality
options.C: Because physical symptoms are rarely important
options.D: So doctors do not have to talk to families

explanation: Looking past the disease allows the nurse to see how home life and social factors impact overall health and recovery. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h1)

question: What happens to a household when one member falls seriously ill?

options.A: Every other member automatically becomes immune
options.B: Daily household chores completely stop forever
options.C: The balance of the whole group is disturbed
options.D: The government takes over all family finances

explanation: Because a family operates as a single system, sickness in one person creates stress and changes for everyone else. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h2)

question: Why should nurses treat the family as the client?

options.A: Hospitals lack enough beds for individual patients
options.B: Families pay the nursing salaries directly each month
options.C: Healing improves when the support system is involved
options.D: It is a strict legal requirement in all wards

explanation: Involving the family ensures better compliance and emotional backing, which speeds up recovery for the patient. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h2)

question: Which family structure includes grandparents and uncles living nearby?
explanation: The extended family structure goes beyond the parents and children to include other relatives like grandparents, aunts, and uncles. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is a major challenge often found in extended family systems during health crises?

options.A: Conflicting medical advice from many relatives
options.B: The inability to ever visit a local hospital
options.C: A complete absence of anyone to care for children
options.D: Strict government bans on shared housing

explanation: While extended families offer great support, having many opinions can sometimes create confusion regarding prescribed medical treatments. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h3)

question: What usually happens to established family roles during a severe illness?

options.A: They remain completely unchanged until discharge
options.B: They are abolished by the hospital management
options.C: They shift and get redistributed among other members
options.D: The government permanently assigns new tasks

explanation: Illness forces other members to take over tasks like earning money or doing chores when the sick person can no longer do them. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h4)

question: Why must nurses watch out for sudden family role reversals?

options.A: To stop relatives from visiting the clinic
options.B: To prevent caregiver burnout and high anxiety
options.C: To ensure the patient pays all hospital bills
options.D: To test the patient's memory after surgery

explanation: Sudden changes in responsibilities cause stress and emotional fatigue, which nurses can help mitigate through counseling and support. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h4)

question: What should a family-centered nursing assessment include?

options.A: Reviewing the medical history of the local doctor
options.B: Counting the number of rooms in the family house
options.C: Checking only the patient's blood pressure and pulse
options.D: Identifying who makes decisions and provides home care

explanation: Knowing who holds decision-making power and who will help at home ensures that care plans are practical and effective. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h5)

question: Why might a treatment plan fail if it requires home refrigeration?

options.A: Medicines lose their color inside cold environments
options.B: Patients refuse to keep drugs near food items
options.C: Refrigerators are illegal in most Nigerian villages
options.D: The family may lack reliable electricity at home

explanation: Nurses must consider home realities like erratic power supply so they can plan alternative storage or treatment methods. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h5)

question: Which group holds strong influence over public health behaviors in many areas?

options.A: Private car drivers passing through towns
options.B: Foreign tourists visiting local holiday resorts
options.C: International sports players and movie stars

explanation: Trusted local figures like chiefs and religious leaders guide community opinions and greatly impact health practices. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h6)

question: Why do public health nurses collaborate with local chiefs and elders?

options.A: Local customs forbid nurses from speaking directly
options.B: Elders are legally trained to write medical prescriptions
options.C: Messages delivered through trusted leaders carry more weight
options.D: Chiefs pay the salaries of community health workers

explanation: People are more likely to accept health campaigns like immunizations when endorsed by figures they already respect and trust. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h6)

question: What is a key duty of public health nurses during discharge planning?

options.A: Building new primary health clinics overnight
options.B: Taking over full legal custody of sick children
options.C: Purchasing personal vehicles for every discharged patient
options.D: Connecting patients to available community resources

explanation: Linking patients to local clinics, NGOs, and support groups ensures continued care after they leave the hospital. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h7)

question: How do community health programs help prevent hospital readmissions?

options.A: By giving free financial loans to all citizens
options.B: By locking hospital gates against returning patients
options.C: By providing ongoing support and disease monitoring at home
options.D: By replacing all doctors with community volunteers

explanation: Continuous home monitoring and health education catch complications early, keeping patients stable outside the hospital. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h7)
